whatIsIt.eli5: Makes a small picture twice as big by copying each dot into a 2×2 block.
whatIsIt.simple: Doubles the height and width of a map by repeating each value in a 2×2 square (nearest neighbour). It has no learned weights.

whyExists.eli5: To mix a small, smart map with a big, detailed map, they first have to be the same size.
whyExists.simple: In the neck's top-down path, the deep, meaningful map is enlarged so it can be joined (Concat) with a larger, more detailed map from the backbone.
whyExists.engineer: FPN top-down pathway: aligns coarse semantic features to the next finer level before lateral concatenation.

eli5: Copy it into a little 2×2 square.
Now the picture is twice as wide and twice as tall.
simple: Each value is repeated 2 times across and 2 times down.
Output height and width are double the input.
engineer: Cheaper than a transposed conv, and free of checkerboard artefacts.

example.simple: YOLOv8n layer 10: 256×20×20 → 256×40×40, ready to join with backbone layer 6 (128×40×40).

typicalPositions.eli5: In the mixing part, going from small maps back to bigger ones.
typicalPositions.simple: Top-down path of the neck, right before each Concat with a backbone map.
